This ordering fences concurrent logout/refresh replay/factor replacement and serializes TOTP replay. Verification failures are counted by anti-abuse; infrastructure/security-unavailable failures do not consume the bad-code budget.

review_notes: Activation first derives a trusted client address and reserves a 30-attempt address budget, then a tighter five-attempt invite-token credential budget. Only an already ACTIVE account with a supported matching password may converge to ALREADY_ACTIVATED; all other cases use the same StaffActivationFailedError. The authoritative DB activation and successful reservation finalization occur in one transaction. Failed credentials count anti-abuse reservations, while successful/idempotent activation reservations are ignored rather than consuming failure budgets.

review_notes: The browser auth surface requires an explicitly allowed Origin on login, refresh and logout, requires JSON and rejects query/body authority outside the strict contracts. Refresh requires an empty body and exactly one refresh cookie name; malformed/missing/duplicate cookie authority is treated as generic authentication failure and clears the browser cookie. A successful refresh rotates the server refresh credential and replaces the cookie with the remaining absolute-session lifetime. Transport/Origin failures occur before credential consumption and therefore do not clear or rotate a valid credential. Logout is intentionally idempotent/non-disclosing, delegates server revocation by refresh credential when present, then clears the cookie.

review_notes: Login performs one Argon2 verification for every account state, using a fixed accepted dummy hash for unknown/passwordless/unsupported stored hashes and the real accepted hash otherwise. Only ACTIVE users with a supported matching password proceed. Before session issuance the transaction takes the per-user security advisory lock and rechecks the exact password hash plus ACTIVE status, fencing concurrent password/status changes. Access and refresh credentials are independent 256-bit random tokens; only domain-separated SHA-256 hashes are persisted. Session/access lifetime is 15 minutes bounded by a fixed 720-hour absolute session expiry, and the refresh expires at the same absolute boundary. Successful login finalizes any identifier anti-abuse reservation inside the same transaction so session creation cannot commit while limiter finalization fails. Refresh validates syntax, hashes the credential, obtains the same user security boundary, then locks refresh/session/user rows. A consumed refresh is treated as replay and atomically revokes the whole session family. Expired/revoked/disabled-user refresh likewise revokes the session. A valid refresh consumes the old credential, creates exactly one next-generation credential expiring at the unchanged absolute session deadline, links replaced_by_credential_id, rotates the access hash and clamps access/cookie lifetime to the absolute expiry. The old access token becomes stale because current_access_token_hash changes. Concurrent same-token refreshes therefore produce one winner and one replay revocation, intentionally invalidating the family after detected reuse.
feature_group: Staff password authentication, opaque session issuance and refresh-family rotation/replay revocation

Projects historical staff names only when both current membership name components are nonempty, canonically trimmed, <=100 Unicode code points and free of isolated UTF-16 surrogate code units. Missing/invalid identity becomes null instead of displaying malformed data.

Input parsing accepts nonnegative canonical decimal strings with at most three fractional digits, converts exactly to bigint mills, and rejects values above the fixed maximum. assertCollectionNotStarted fails closed when canonical payment shows any paid amount, PENDING/PAID status, provider or provider reference, or repository-level collection evidence. It is invoked before guest/staff tip and precollection financial corrections/validation paths, preventing terms from changing after collection has begun even if the current payment row alone has not reached PAID.

review_notes: The repository locks the canonical payment by organization/location/session FOR UPDATE and validation history by organization/payment FOR UPDATE, serializing same-payment mutations. Collection evidence checks any cash entry, provider event or durable collection operation, so even an incomplete/failed collection attempt freezes mutable financial terms. Validation replacement clears only the currently locked prior row before inserting the new current row. updatePaymentTerms rewrites precollection terms and clears provider/reference/paidAt from a trusted locked payment; callers first enforce collection-not-started and recompute exact money. projectMutation returns the bounded mutation view.

Reconciliation first resolves the operation only within the authenticated provider binding organization, locks the related session/payment/operation, and requires an unresolved dispatched state, matching provider, compatible stable reference, exact currency/amount snapshot, zero paid amount, null paidAt and UNPAID/FAILED payment. A provider reference must be present and unowned elsewhere. The operation CAS to RESOLVED and guarded payment projection to PAID/FAILED occur in one transaction; a failed payment update throws so the operation transition rolls back. Reordered failures cannot downgrade PAID, PREPARED/REJECTED/RESOLVED operations cannot revive, and a definitive failure permits a later fresh guarded collection attempt.

The callback boundary exposes only rejected versus processing-failed outcomes with fixed messages. Refund callback authority begins from the authenticated binding organization, resolves only that tenant's refund/payment, locks the session/payment/refund, and accepts transitions only from PENDING with null completedAt and matching provider/reference. The guarded UPDATE moves the refund once to SUCCEEDED with completedAt or FAILED without completedAt and never rewrites the canonical payment collection facts.

Committed-event dedup is keyed by authenticated organization/provider/providerEventId. Collection/refund correlation lookup is tenant scoped before identities are exposed. Shared API error envelope is strict and requires non-empty code/message plus a bounded 1-128 character requestId limited to safe token characters, preventing arbitrary response metadata from crossing the common error boundary.

Common investigation tests reject invalid/offset/local timestamps, contradictory current labels, person email leakage, source-coverage metadata widening, client-injected role authority, raw plate in cursor payload, wrong cursor purpose/precision, and cursor lifetime beyond 15 minutes.

Issue #300 common contracts separate public safe labels/persons/references/coverage from server-only read scope and signed cursor payload. Cursors are purpose-discriminated, session/scope/filter/snapshot bound, microsecond-keyset precise, strict, and limited to 15 minutes while comments explicitly forbid PII/filter text/credentials/raw metadata.

Detail tests constrain path source to the known catalog, reject free-form routing/raw incident description/private dispatch reason, require source/key agreement, and permit null key slot only for the authentic RELEASED custody event rather than slot-required custody kinds.

Strict source-discriminated detail projection exposes only bounded common evidence plus approved source-specific facts. Audit unknown kinds remain metadata-free, incidents expose current status/type/severity only, and super-refinement prevents source/key mismatch and invalid slot-less custody facts.

Selector-directory tests enforce purpose-limited MEMBER/KEY_SLOT searches, text <=80, page <=20, no email-query flag, and response items containing only exact ID plus current safe label with no contact fields.

Filter contract allows only MEMBER/KEY_SLOT kind, bounded optional text, opaque cursor and max-20 page. Exact Location is deliberately absent from client overrides; responses expose only ID/current label and enforce continuation consistency.

Search tests reject organization/client-authority and metadata query fields, cap limit at 100 and window at positive <=31 elapsed days, reject fabricated total counts, and preserve the semantic distinction between current vehicle/state labels and typed historical match witnesses.

Search contract supports bounded AND-style discovery filters over a 31-day UTC window while excluding scope/authority fields. Results separate current vehicle/key-slot/session facts from historical match reasons, bound counts/reasons/pages, and expose explicit per-source coverage instead of implying completeness.

Timeline tests keep the canonical full timeline distinct from discovery-window filters, cap pages at 100, require canonical source/event IDs, reject raw evidence metadata and unsafe references, force ASC ordering, and expose current actor/vehicle labels only through approved safe projections.

Timeline contract deliberately has no discovery from/to filters: it reads one canonical session timeline with opaque cursor and max-100 page. Events are source-discriminated, expose only approved actor/current vehicle/reference/coverage facts, and the response is strict with ASC order plus continuation consistency.

Pre-custody cancellation tests require exact task/shift IDs and positive session/task versions, reject client-supplied organization/state/actor authority, and require canonical status evidence rather than treating a missing task as successful cancellation. Response widening with PII is rejected.

Cancellation wire contract carries only task identity, expected session/task versions and expected shift. Status projection distinguishes CANCELLED from NOT_CANCELLED with PRE_CUSTODY/ADVANCED classification and minimal versioned session/task evidence, with strict objects throughout.

Incomplete Check-In cancellation tests enforce exact expected lifecycle version/shift and reject actor/state/reason/org/timestamp authority fields. Terminal response is minimal, and the tests explicitly prove CANCELLED is not widened into guest-safe or active staff-directory contracts.

Strict Check-In cancellation request carries only expected version and expected shift; terminal response returns session/location/version with literal CANCELLED, while the reconciliation status response uses the canonical staff valet-session state catalog without extra evidence or secrets.

Shared Check-In identity contracts distinguish human-confirmed plate from temporary descriptor and make vehicle details strict. Detail strings are trimmed/NFKC-normalized and bounded to 80 Unicode code points; deeper identity normalization/bounds are also revalidated by server vehicle-identity logic before persistence.

Guest-access tests pin raw guest credentials to exactly 32 CSPRNG bytes encoded as 43 unpadded base64url characters and reject padding/non-base64url/non-string material. Guest-safe session readiness accepts canonical UTC timestamps and strict projection rejects organization scope leakage.

Phone tests accept employee presentation variants for Jordan mobiles and normalize them to one canonical +9627xxxxxxxx wire value, while malformed lengths/prefixes/text are rejected. DIFFERENT_CUSTOMER accepts only the canonical wire form.

Check-In transport contracts are strict across intake/customer intent, vehicle identity/details, condition evidence, guest-access issue/revoke, completion and guest-safe session/branding projections. Although several raw wire strings are intentionally broad, caller inspection confirms the server re-normalizes before persistence: intake operation IDs are constrained to 8-128 safe characters, display name to 120 code points, vehicle identity/details to domain limits, and condition notes to bounded non-control text.

Company analytics tests require truthful null metrics for empty samples, explicit coverage, weighted aggregate counts without per-employee disclosure, deterministic timezone ordering, bounded grouping arrays, and reject guest-rating/returning-contact/byEmployee or malformed numeric widening.

Company analytics response is an aggregate-only strict projection with explicit location/timezone coverage, bounded operational/financial/incident groups, fixed-precision ratios, and KPI evidence counts. It deliberately omits staff-level breakdown and contact/guest identity data while reusing controlled location analytics schemas.

Company report tests require DAILY reports to include only controlled dispatch/key-custody aggregate activity, keep WEEKLY/MONTHLY free of daily activity, bound event groups to their catalogs, reuse the company analytics summary, and allow only existing CSV/PDF export requests while rejecting XLSX or contact inclusion.

Company report contracts reuse existing bounded period/export schemas and company aggregate summary. DAILY adds only aggregate retrieval, dispatch and key-custody counts; WEEKLY/MONTHLY carry no raw daily activity, with strict envelopes and organization/date fields.

Complete-handoff tests limit the mutation request to expected session version only and require a minimal terminal projection where retrieval request, task and session all agree on COMPLETED. Extra verification/internal identifiers are rejected.
Strict handoff completion contract uses only optimistic session version input and returns the exact terminal session/task projection without custody secret, proof, actor or scope material.

Condition-photo tests validate the complete PENDING/VERIFIED/EXPIRED/REJECTED state machine, byte/retry/timestamp bounds, exact-session state discovery, multipart metadata restricted to operationId, empty reconciliation/query contracts, and explicit rejection of storage URLs/keys/hashes/lease/auth/scope/user metadata from public responses.

Verified-photo wire v1 is intentionally provider-neutral and strict: 8MiB JPEG cap, bounded retry advice, safe public error catalog, state-discriminated operation results, operationId-only multipart metadata, empty reconcile/query bodies, policy source limited to organization default/location override, and state discovery binds operation evidence to the exact valet session.

Confirm Parked tests require session/task CAS versions, trimmed nonempty key-slot code and exactly one parking resource code, with optional spot ID only alongside spot code. Success projection is terminal/minimal and deliberately excludes key-slot detail.

Confirm Parked contract carries only optimistic versions plus key-slot and one parking resource identity, with refinements preventing contradictory resource shapes. Server consumer inspection confirms codes are resolved under authoritative organization/location, active/compatibility/occupancy locks and parameterized SQL before parking state commits.

Feedback analytics tests enforce truthful completed/rated cohort arithmetic, null semantics, 1-5 rating bounds, participation/average consistency, at most four recent rows, and a pseudonymous VISIT reference while rejecting guest phone/name/internal session identity and unsupported scope.

Customer feedback analytics is a strict COMPANY/LOCATION aggregate projection with nonnegative safe counts, fixed-precision average/participation, bounded 1-5 distribution, and four recent pseudonymous rows carrying only visit reference, rating, timestamps, authorized location label and timezone. Super-refinement enforces cohort arithmetic.

Feature-authority tests keep Visit Contacts organization-scoped, allow Management Audit organization or exact-location queries, and validate only truthful role/scope projections: org admin organization, location manager grant-set for Visit Contacts, and exact-location authority for Management Audit including permitted supervisor scope.

Dashboard feature-authority contract strictly models only VISIT_CONTACTS and MANAGEMENT_AUDIT, validates feature-specific query scope, and constrains server responses to ORG_ADMIN/LOCATION_MANAGER/VALET_SUPERVISOR with ORGANIZATION, ORGANIZATION_GRANT_SET or exact LOCATION combinations that are valid for that feature.

Dispatch tests cover self/explicit/automatic assignment shapes, reject client organization/membership query authority and conflicting automatic target, normalize/bound reasons, keep task projections minimal, strictly constrain queue vehicle fields, and require tracking to be explicit opt-in with a privacy-minimal movement projection.

Dispatch contracts use strict versioned task projections, a safe staff queue vehicle descriptor, location-scoped queue query with explicit tracking opt-in, privacy-minimal tracking projection, and strict assign/accept/decline/reassign requests. CANCELLED valet sessions are excluded from active task-queue items.

Adds VALET_SUPERVISOR and required location timezone/currency; currency is constrained to uppercase three-letter form. This migration assumes existing locations are backfilled/absent when adding NOT NULL columns, consistent with its early-foundation ordering.

Creates parking_spots/key_slots with location-scoped codes and composite tenant/location FKs. Later session and zone migrations add the composite resource keys needed by custody/session references; current schema retains the tenant/location binding.

Restores three read-path indexes for location/state, vehicle history, and location retrieval ordering. No mutation or authorization semantics are introduced.

Creates tenant/location-scoped audit_events with optional session/actor references and session timeline index. Later audit-foundation migrations add actor typing, append-only/runtime privileges and stricter write guards; current writers use atomic transaction boundaries with domain mutations.

Defines one payment per tenant/session, payment state/method shape, nonnegative money, provider-reference uniqueness, and versioned current validation history. Composite FKs prevent cross-tenant payment/validation references; later payment-operation migrations harden write authority and transitions.

Creates append-style cash ledger rows and provider-event ingress records. Cash entry amounts are positive with reasons required for adjustments; idempotency is organization-scoped and a partial unique index prevents duplicate RECEIPT per payment.

Adds tenant/payment-bound refund records, authorization actor, retry key and provider correlation; then safely enables provider events to point at a refund within the same organization/payment. Status/provider/completion constraints distinguish asynchronous provider refunds from succeeded local records.

Creates incident records separately from session state with tenant/location/session and reporter/resolver membership FKs. Reporting code inserts OPEN incidents plus audit atomically; later recovery/resolution work adds controlled mutation authority and recovery-intent durability.

Creates notification delivery state independently from session state with organization/session ownership and required terminal timestamps for SENT/FAILED. Current outbound messaging paths consume the table while newer push persistence uses separate records.

Adds company/location photo policy, paired condition-completion fields, append/supersede condition notes, and private vehicle-photo metadata with tenant/location/session/capturer binding. Supersession is constrained to the same session/context and storage keys are globally unique.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

Persists hashed staff access/refresh credentials with bounded expiry, monotonic refresh generations, one unconsumed refresh per session, and same-session replacement linkage. Current auth service rotates/revokes through these records; MFA is added later without weakening these token hashes.

Creates durable hashed anti-abuse counters with a closed scope/state allowlist and an indexed one-hour retention cleanup. Cleanup is SECURITY DEFINER with fixed search_path and PUBLIC execution revoked; later migrations extend allowed scopes deliberately.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

Establishes Task lifecycle separately from ValetSession and append-style dispatch events. A partial unique index prevents multiple active tasks of the same type per session; task/session/location and event/task FKs carry the tenant/location/session scope into dispatch history.

Replaces requester consistency so CUSTOMER retrieval requests cannot carry a staff membership, while STAFF requests require a membership and cannot carry a customer id. Customer identity remains optional because guest-token/browser-session flows can legitimately request retrieval without a persisted Customer row.

Adds company-default/location-override handoff method policy and extends the durable anti-abuse allowlist for handoff issuance/verification session scopes. This preserves typed Configuration First precedence and explicit anti-abuse classification.

Adds opt-in tracking policy, map geometry, task-scoped tracking sessions, raw GPS samples and geofence events with nested composite scope FKs. Active tracking is unique per task and per valet session; ended_at can only transition once, and GPS coordinates are DB-bounded.

Defines SECURITY DEFINER map-setup commands that derive organization authority from the actor/location instead of caller-supplied tenant ids. Functions use fixed search_path, active org/location/user/membership plus location access, LOCATION_MANAGER role, row locking/CAS on updates, bounded geometry/labels, same-scope parking-zone validation, and audit writes; PUBLIC execution is revoked for every helper/command.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

Adds typed company-default/location-override financial policy for fee, payer, payment methods, tips, validation and release gating. Fee values are nonnegative and the current resolver applies location overrides over company defaults.

Adds an immutable end-of-shift cash reconciliation snapshot to shifts. The DB requires complete-or-empty reconciliation data, nonnegative expected/reported amounts, exact variance arithmetic, currency shape, the reporting membership to equal the shift owner, and the reconciliation timestamp to equal ended_at on an ENDED shift.

Introduces durable digital collection operation state for crash/unknown-outcome recovery. State/data checks distinguish PREPARED, guarded unknown outcome, provider-reference attachment, rejection, and resolution; unique submission and provider-reference keys provide idempotency, while a partial unique index permits only one unresolved operation for a payment.

Creates narrow Location Manager SECURITY DEFINER configuration commands. Authority is derived from an active actor/user/organization/location plus explicit location access and LOCATION_MANAGER role; values are type/currency-precision validated, the location row is locked, expected_updated_at provides CAS, updated_at advances monotonically, and every mutation appends old/new effective-state audit metadata.

Adds basic branding overrides plus typed organization subscription entitlements and LM branding commands. Branding mutation authority mirrors the location-configuration boundary with active LM/location access checks, row lock/CAS, canonical text/color validation and atomic audit. The original color SET NULL ambiguity in this migration is explicitly corrected by the immediately following forward-only hardening migration 031.

Forward-only hardening closes NULL-as-clear on primary-color SET and normalizes existing display-name overrides before replacing the check with canonical outer-trim enforcement. Dedicated CLEAR remains the only supported override removal path.

Defines staff push registrations, tenant/session/task-scoped intents and deliveries with registration/delivery state-machine guards, lease fencing, retry bounds, terminal shapes and dedupe indexes. Registration rows are account-session scoped rather than tenant scoped; the delivery writer and worker eligibility query bind the registration's staff-auth user back to the exact recipient membership, organization, location access and active shift before any provider send.

Adds bounded SKIP LOCKED cleanup for terminal deliveries, orphaned old intents and terminal registrations, with dependency checks preventing deletion of still-referenced rows. Cleanup is SECURITY DEFINER with fixed search_path and PUBLIC execution revoked; runtime provisioning explicitly controls cleanup execution.

Reserves UUIDv8 incident identities for crash-recovery intent, rejects any legacy collision during migration, and persists a 15-minute tenant/location/session/reporter-bound RESERVED intent that can transition exactly once to RETIRED. Trigger-authored timing prevents callers from extending expiry or rewriting bindings.

Extends tenant audit events with typed actor provenance and introduces a separate append-only account-security audit stream. The audit actor CHECK is deliberately NOT VALID so legacy null-actor history remains readable, while PostgreSQL still enforces it for new/updated rows; investigation queries explicitly preserve legacy null-as-membership semantics. Account-security append uses a stable-id advisory lock and exact idempotent replay comparison.

Adds protected TOTP factor state, ten-slot versioned recovery-code sets and exact-session MFA assurance fields. DB guards make factor identity/secret immutable, prevent ACTIVE->PENDING or RETIRED reactivation, enforce monotonically advancing accepted TOTP steps and recovery generation, and make recovery verifiers immutable except one-way consumption.

Introduces versioned Staff Management mutation commands with organization serialization, actor/target row locks, last-usable-admin protection, operational handover blockers, bounded tenant-scoped access arrays and CAS. Later LM-authority/onboarding migrations CREATE OR REPLACE these three commands, so current behavior was checked against the replacement chain rather than treating this historical body as final.

Adds five typed settings plus seven-day company/location operating-hours persistence and consolidates ORG_ADMIN company/location settings and branding commands. Organization advisory serialization precedes row/CAS mutation, company-default fee changes validate every inheriting location's currency precision, location overrides preserve Company->Location precedence, operating hours require exactly seven distinct weekdays and valid same-day intervals, and audit captures canonical old/new values. The migration also strengthens existing LM configuration/branding helpers with the same organization settings lock.
Adds the organization + occurred_at DESC + id DESC index used for deterministic management audit pagination. It changes only query performance/order support and introduces no new write authority.

Introduces explicit location intake fencing and narrow ORG_ADMIN lifecycle commands. New locations start INACTIVE/not accepting intake; activation validates timezone/currency readiness, stop-intake precedes drain/deactivation, blockers cover live sessions/shifts/tasks, and currency/timezone corrections require an inactive drained location with CAS. Audit event types are protected from generic runtime forgery. A later issue-346 migration adds the currently provisioned resume-intake command and extends the audit guard.

Adds query indexes and two narrow ORG_ADMIN customer contact correction commands. Both lock the exact tenant-owned Customer, support convergent exact retries before stale-token conflict, advance updated_at monotonically and append non-PII correction audit metadata atomically. Phone corrections are explicitly limited to the Jordan mobile normalization contract used by this feature.

The script explicitly requires psql no-transaction execution and ON_ERROR_STOP because CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run in a transaction. TOTP factor insertion includes protected_secret but later UPDATE excludes it; mutable fields are lifecycle state, last accepted TOTP step, recovery generation and activation/retirement times. review_notes: Under the supplied restricted runtime role the smoke requires PostgreSQL 42501 when attempting to create an enabled/verified Meta binding or explicitly set enabled, provider verification evidence, revision or timestamps. A safe insert omitting protected columns must converge to disabled, unverified, revision=1 defaults. Runtime is also denied operator-only verification UPDATE while allowed to edit config_alias and increment revision/updated_at.
feature_group: Outbound provider-binding API-role self-attestation regression smoke

review_notes: Seven DISPATCHING-expired-lease scenarios distinguish signed provider SENT/DELIVERED/READ, signed FAILED, a forged delivery timestamp, a bare stored provider message id and no proof. Recovery under sender role must terminalize all: only authenticated successful callback events become ACCEPTED; failed/forged/bare/absent evidence becomes UNKNOWN. Every path clears lease/retry, purges encrypted envelope, and repeat recovery is idempotent with zero rows; recovered deliveries cannot be claimed for resend.
feature_group: Outbound dispatch crash recovery authenticated-proof fencing smoke

review_notes: Synthetic setup exercises restricted intake helpers under runtime role while direct customer/permission/control/event reads are denied. Cross-organization permission lookup returns empty, duplicate intent hits uniqueness, and cross-tenant delivery linkage hits FK failure. With sending disabled no delivery is claimable. Once enabled, dispatch permit rejects wrong recipient digest; post-permit confirmation rejects changed supplied phone, changed canonical customer phone and policy revision drift. Provider callback rejects wrong recipient, accepts/deduplicates the correct signed event, and later NOT_SENT finalization cannot downgrade callback-first delivered state. Successful terminalization purges envelope.
feature_group: Outbound tenant, permission, send-fence, callback-dedupe and purge constraint smoke

review_notes: The smoke constructs a NOT_SENT attempt with delivery already in RETRY_WAIT and an encrypted envelope, then records a signed SENT provider event. Expected convergence is ACCEPTED, next_attempt_at cleared, envelope deleted, and delivery absent from the due-claim set. This protects against duplicate outbound sends when provider acknowledgement arrives after local retry scheduling.
feature_group: Late authenticated callback cancels scheduled outbound retry

review_notes: The smoke creates an intent while only Company policy applies, claims its delivery, then inserts a Location override disabling INITIAL_GUEST_ACCESS. The already-leased outbound_dispatch_permit must fail with P0001 despite the earlier intent snapshot, proving the final send gate re-evaluates current effective policy. The fixture then suppresses the synthetic row to avoid contaminating later smoke cases.
feature_group: Late Location policy override invalidates an already-issued outbound intent

review_notes: The runner refuses non-local PostgreSQL hosts, creates a uniquely named disposable database, applies every migration in lexical order, asserts exactly 12 outbound tables and OFF/OFF control defaults, provisions isolated runtime/sender/webhook roles, then deliberately reproduces the historical vulnerable full-table provider-binding INSERT grant and applies forward migration 090 to prove in-place ACL repair. It re-verifies runtime privileges and runs all outbound constraint/race/recovery/phone/consent smokes before forcibly dropping the database and generated roles in finally blocks.
feature_group: Disposable PostgreSQL full outbound migration/ACL regression harness

review_notes: The smoke creates a PENDING scheduled delivery plus encrypted envelope, records a WITHDRAW permission revision, and invokes recovery. Expected convergence is one recovered row in SUPPRESSED with next_attempt_at null and envelope count zero; the suppressed delivery must not appear in outbound_claim_due. This verifies revocation takes effect after issuance and removes both retry eligibility and retained message ciphertext.
feature_group: Consent withdrawal suppresses pending outbound delivery and purges ciphertext

review_notes: The smoke exercises PENDING, LEASED, RETRY_WAIT and DISPATCHING rows against customer phone changes. A transactional change proves suppression is rollback-safe; a no-op update preserves rows; committed drift immediately SUPPRESSES and purges undispatched rows while in-flight DISPATCHING remains fenced until lease recovery converges to UNKNOWN. F33 cases prove recipient_routing_uncertain is monotone and cannot be manually cleared, arbitrary DISPATCHING->RETRY_WAIT without a finalized matching negative attempt is rejected by CHECK/guard, changed-phone definitive failure or NOT_SENT converges to SUPPRESSED, changed-phone UNKNOWN stays UNKNOWN, ACCEPTED stays accepted, and an authenticated positive callback cannot be downgraded by a later definitive failure. Same-phone definitive/NOT_SENT can retain bounded retry until a later phone change suppresses it.
feature_group: Outbound canonical phone drift and post-dispatch retry fencing regression smoke

review_notes: Sender and webhook receive disjoint approved SECURITY DEFINER function surfaces: sender can claim/lease/permit/confirm/finalize/recover/cleanup deliveries, while webhook can only resolve Meta binding and record provider events. Provisioning rejects principals that cannot login, are superuser/createdb/createrole/replication/bypassrls, inherit roles, hold memberships, or own public objects. It grants CONNECT+schema USAGE, explicitly removes database CREATE/TEMP and all table/sequence/function authority, then grants only approved functions. Verification requires zero table privileges over all 12 outbound tables, exact function access by principal kind, and no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on valet_sessions/customers/guest_browser_sessions/audit_events.
feature_group: Dedicated outbound sender/webhook database principal hardening

review_notes: A synthetic DISPATCHING delivery with expired lease, active attempt and encrypted envelope but no authenticated callback is recovered exactly once. Required result is delivery UNKNOWN, attempt UNKNOWN, lease token cleared and envelope purged; outbound_claim_due must never return it. The design prefers terminal uncertainty over automatic resend when provider acceptance is unknowable.
feature_group: Stale in-flight outbound recovery without trusted provider evidence

review_notes: The smoke creates runtime/sender/webhook roles with LOGIN, NOINHERIT and all elevated PostgreSQL attributes disabled, provisions the API runtime and the dedicated sender/webhook principals, and verifies all three cannot SELECT the encrypted envelope table. It also checks sender/webhook cannot UPDATE valet_sessions/customers and performs a real SET ROLE sender arbitrary ciphertext SELECT expecting 42501.
feature_group: Disposable role creation and effective outbound privilege smoke

review_notes: Provisioning revokes PUBLIC/runtime access across all 12 outbound tables, grants SELECT only on bindings/policies/control/permissions/intents/deliveries and INSERT only on policies/intents/deliveries/envelopes. Provider-binding insertion is intentionally column-scoped to onboarding identity/config fields, repairing the prior table-wide self-attestation vulnerability; enabled/verification evidence/revision/timestamps cannot be inserted. Binding UPDATE is limited to enabled/revision/updated_at/config_alias, while sensitive organization/phone scope is not updatable; policy UPDATE excludes organization/location and global send control. API runtime gets only permission-change and scoped intake read functions, never sender/webhook dispatch functions. Verification rechecks table ACLs including PUBLIC, exact binding INSERT columns, restricted update columns, and exact function surface.
feature_group: Ordinary API outbound data/function least-privilege provisioning

review_notes: The runtime may SELECT and INSERT payment_collection_operations but has no table-wide UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER. Only lifecycle/reconciliation fields state, provider_reference, safe_result_code, dispatch_guarded_at, resolved_at and updated_at receive UPDATE authority. Provisioning revokes PUBLIC and role table authority before restoring SELECT/INSERT plus those column updates.

API error tests exercise parsed known status/error code fallback, network failure classification and request metadata. Parsing remains in api-error.ts; unknown mutation outcomes must not be treated as definitive failures.

Preserves status/code/message/requestId/retryAfter/network marker. Normalization prefers the shared strict API-error schema, then a bounded legacy object with a string code, otherwise derives a stable code from HTTP status. Dedicated network, session-service-unavailable and authentication-required constructors keep failure classes distinct.

Generation-scoped concurrent authenticated reads share one refresh/renewal attempt while preventing stale-auth reuse; tests deliberately model overlapped read requests and auth transition. The server owns bearer/session truth.

Cancellation test scenarios assert PREPARE before user-confirmed POST, one outbound mutation, response and status reconciliation for ambiguous results, no automatic retry, plus authorization/scope/background/identity generation retirement.

Binding captures auth generation plus exact operational scope/role. Prepare accepts only the requested session at the current location in CHECKING_IN and captures shift/version. Confirm dispatches one POST and requires exact session/location/version+1.
